wastewater.blower_air_shortfall.name: Blower air shortfall starving the aeration basin
wastewater.blower_air_shortfall.archetype: 05 Component degradation (seen as 07: symptom on the stage, cause on its blower)
wastewater.blower_air_shortfall.summary: Dissolved oxygen sliding below the nitrification range while the air the stage is actually getting falls behind the other five trains. Following the air_flow layer back to the blower shows air flow and discharge pressure falling together — the signature of a restriction on the blower's own side, not a plugged diffuser and not an oxygen demand spike.

pipeline.text: diffuser grid → its blower; read the blower's own flow and discharge pressure

pipeline.title: Locate the cause
pipeline.text: flow down AND discharge pressure down = supply-side restriction; flow down with pressure up would be the diffusers

pipeline.title: Rule out demand
pipeline.text: F:M and MLSS inside the plant band — if demand had risen, air would have risen too

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the cause is the blower; recovery after the filter was cleared → high

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: A restriction on the T03 Blower's own side cut air delivery 28 %; the DO collapse in the basin followed from it
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: air and DO recovered when the blower was cleared

series.label: Median of the other five trains

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Dissolved oxygen in T03's aeration basin against the median of the other five trains, which take the same influent. The shaded gap is the oxygen the basin should have had.

checks.label: Dissolved oxygen below the nitrification floor, and it stayed there
checks.value: 2.07 mg/L at 08:40 down to 0.59 mg/L at 10:45; under 1.5 mg/L from 09:30 for 1 h 35 min. Flagged at 10:00, after 30 min under the floor.
checks.why: Nitrifiers need about 2.0 mg/L to work reliably and start to fail below 1.5 mg/L. A short dip is normal; 1 h 35 min under the floor is lost nitrification.

checks.label: Getting less air than the other five trains
checks.value: Header air 3,101 scfm against a peer median of 4,144 scfm at 10:45 — 75 %. Below 88 % from 09:20; the other trains held 94–100 % of their own peer median.
checks.why: All six trains take the same influent on the same diurnal curve, so they need similar air. A train that drops out of the pack is short of air, not short of demand.

checks.label: The Blower: air flow and discharge pressure fell together
checks.value: Blower air flow 1,907 → 1,381 scfm (−28 %, 526 scfm of air lost) and discharge pressure 7.75 → 6.41 psi (−17 %).
checks.why: Walking the air_flow layer back from the diffuser grid lands on this blower. On a system curve, less air means less friction loss, so a blower that can't draw enough air shows lower flow AND lower discharge pressure. A blockage downstream of the blower would push the pressure up instead.

checks.label: Oxygen demand did not spike
checks.value: F:M 0.265–0.324 and MLSS 2,509–2,958 mg/L all shift, both inside the conventional band.
checks.why: If the incoming load had risen, the DO controller would have called for MORE air and the header would have gone up. Air went down while the load sat still, so the air side is the problem.

checks.label: Blower running hotter
checks.value: Blower discharge temperature 71.8 → 85.0 °C (+13.2 °C) over the same window.
checks.why: A separate sensor. Pulling air through a restriction raises the pressure ratio across the machine, and discharge temperature goes with the pressure ratio. It also rules out a flow-meter fault: a bad meter would not warm the blower.

checks.label: Diffuser Grid backpressure fell with the air
checks.value: Backpressure 1.31 → 0.91 psi (−31 %) and air distribution 90.9 → 86.1 % (−4.8 points).
checks.why: Separate sensors on the grid itself. Less air through the same holes means less backpressure, and coverage falls off below about 95 % of design air. Fouled diffusers would do the opposite: backpressure up at less air.

checks.label: The other five trains were fine
checks.value: Their lowest DO over the same window was 1.68–1.85 mg/L (T01, T02, T04, T05 and T06), each within 94–100 % of its own peer median for air.
checks.why: The six trains share the influent, the weather and the plant air main. Only this one lost air, so it is not a plant-wide blower-house or influent event.

checks.label: Settling got worse while DO was low
checks.value: Secondary TSS removal averaged 87.2 % while DO was under 1.5 mg/L against 88.7 % outside that window (−1.6 points).
checks.why: A separate measurement a stage downstream. Starved of oxygen the floc goes pin-point and carries over the weirs, so the clarifier confirms the aeration basin really was short of air.

checks.label: Air and DO came back once the blower was worked on
checks.value: "Blower intake filter inspection" completed 10:52; Blower air back to 1,980 scfm (104 % of baseline) at 10:55 and DO back above 1.5 mg/L at 11:05.
checks.why: Air returning the moment the blower was cleared ties the DO loss to the blower and nothing else. Nothing in the basin was changed.

references.title: Blower inlet filter blinding over a shift
references.description: Dust and pollen load the inlet filter. Air flow falls steadily over hours, discharge pressure and diffuser backpressure fall with it, discharge temperature climbs, and DO follows the air down. The filter ΔP gauge reads high; a clean filter restores everything in minutes.
notes: Same steady air decline, not a step
Air and backpressure down together — a supply-side restriction
Blower discharge temperature up +13.2 °C

charts.title: Air delivered, % of normal (h from onset)

references.title: Filter just starting to load
references.description: A few percent of air lost over the shift. DO stays inside the band because the controller has headroom, and only the inlet ΔP gauge and the air flow trend show it. This is where a filter change costs nothing.
notes: T03 lost 28 % of its air, not a few percent
DO had already left the band

charts.title: Air delivered, % of normal (h from onset)

references.title: Fouled fine-bubble diffusers
references.description: Biofilm and scale inside the diffuser membranes. DO falls the same way and air flow falls too, but the blower has to push harder: discharge pressure and diffuser backpressure both rise. The fix is a diffuser clean, not a filter.
notes: Here backpressure fell 31 %, it did not rise
Here discharge pressure fell 17 %

charts.title: Air delivered, % of normal (h from onset)

ruledOut.cause: An oxygen demand spike in the incoming flow
ruledOut.reason: F:M stayed 0.265–0.324 and MLSS 2,509–2,958 mg/L. More demand would have pulled more air; the header fell 28 % instead.

ruledOut.cause: Fouled or plugged diffusers
ruledOut.reason: Diffuser Grid backpressure went DOWN 31 % and the blower's discharge pressure down 17 %. Plugged diffusers raise both.

ruledOut.cause: DO probe fault
ruledOut.reason: Four other instruments moved with it: header air flow, blower discharge pressure, blower discharge temperature (+13.2 °C) and diffuser backpressure. A drifting probe moves alone.

ruledOut.cause: A plant-wide air or influent event
ruledOut.reason: T01, T02, T04, T05 and T06 never went below 1.68 mg/L on normal air through the same window.

ruledOut.cause: Blower mechanical damage (bearing, impeller, drive)
ruledOut.reason: Blower vibration moved +0.32 mm/s from its early-shift level — no bearing or rotor signature. The temperature rise fits a pressure-ratio change, which a restriction explains, and air returned as soon as the machine was cleared.

ruledOut.cause: Why the filter loaded this fast
ruledOut.reason: Inlet filter differential pressure is not instrumented in this model, so how fast it blinded has to come off the local gauge and the filter itself. Worth knowing before the next change interval is set.

confidence.because: The symptom (DO) and the cause (air flow, discharge pressure, discharge temperature) are separate instruments on separate assets, they all moved together, and everything came back when the Blower was cleared.
confidence.lowerIf: Air stays low with a clean filter. Then check the inlet silencer, the butterfly valve position and the blower itself.
confidence.confirmedBy: Air back at 10:55 and DO above the floor at 11:05, after the inlet filter was cleared at 10:52

action.text: Clear the blower intake filter and confirm air flow recovers; monitor DO closely for the next two hours.

model.formula: median of the other five aeration stages at the same time point
model.fittedOn: the other five trains — no coefficients; they share the influent and the diurnal flow curve

WSIT08.impact: 1 h 35 min below 1.5 mg/L, bottoming at 0.59 mg/L. Secondary TSS removal ran 1.6 points lower through the event, and T03 health dropped to 93.8 %. Nitrification lost during a low-DO period takes hours of good DO to rebuild.

conclusion.label: Most likely cause
conclusion.text: A settling change in T01's sludge — filamentous bulking is the leading candidate — with nothing hydraulic or mechanical behind it

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Sludge volume index on T01's secondary clarifier against its own start of shift and the other five trains. T01 has climbed 47 mL/g since 09:20; the rest are where they started.

checks.label: SVI past the 130 mL/g watch level and holding
checks.value: 142.1 mL/g now, above 130 mL/g since 12:10 (1 h 55 min). Flagged at 12:55.
checks.why: Well-settling sludge sits under about 120 mL/g; above 150 mL/g it is bulking and carries over the weirs. In between is the window where a change still costs nothing.

checks.label: Up against its own start of shift
checks.value: 95.0 mL/g over the first 1 h to 142.1 mL/g now (+47.1 mL/g). Left its baseline at 09:20.
checks.why: An SVI level on its own can be a train's normal. A rise of this size against the same clarifier earlier the same shift is a change in the sludge.

checks.label: Climbing all shift, not drifting
checks.value: +9.3 mL/g per hour over the last 4 h, +6.7 mL/g per hour over the last 2 hours. Flag level is +4 mL/g per hour.
checks.why: A settling change in the biology develops over hours to days and keeps going. Normal SVI scatter wanders up and down and nets out near zero over four hours.

checks.label: RAS rate never changed
checks.value: +0.14 % per hour across the whole window (flag level is 2.5), 48.1 % over the first 2 hours against 48.8 % over the last 2. Range 42.6–53.4 %, inside the 25–75 % normal band all shift.
checks.why: Returning less sludge thins the blanket and lifts the apparent SVI. RAS held still, so the number is telling us about the sludge and not about the pump.

checks.label: Nothing changed in the mechanism
checks.value: Clarifier torque +0.08 points per hour across the window (flag level is 2.5), range 46.0–56.1 %.
checks.why: A rising blanket or a dragging mechanism shows up as torque. Flat torque says the clarifier is doing the same mechanical work on a sludge that settles worse.

checks.label: Clarified effluent getting worse with it
checks.value: Secondary TSS removal 88.7 % over the first 1 h against 87.1 % over the last hour (−1.6 points). The other five clarifiers moved −0.6 to +1.0 points over the same two windows (a positive number is a gain), so this is the only one that lost ground.
checks.why: A separate measurement, and the one that matters for the permit. Sludge that settles more slowly leaves more solids in the overflow, which is exactly what this shows.

checks.label: A smooth climb, not test scatter
checks.value: Largest single 5-minute change 1.26 mL/g, against 4.6–6.9 mL/g on the other five clarifiers.
checks.why: Settleability changes as the floc changes, which is slow. A sampling or settleometer problem jumps between readings.

checks.label: The other five clarifiers are flat
checks.value: T02, T03, T04, T05 and T06 ended within −9.0 to +7.0 mL/g of their own first hour; the biggest mover was T04 at +7.0 mL/g.
checks.why: All six trains share the influent. A septic or nutrient-poor influent would push every clarifier; only this one moved.

checks.label: Loading and inventory normal in this train
checks.value: MLSS 2,559–3,040 mg/L, F:M 0.258–0.313, sludge age 8.0–9.5 days — all inside the conventional bands.
checks.why: Rules out the easy explanations: too much solids inventory, an F:M swing, or sludge held far too long. The aeration side is running where it should be.

checks.label: Microscopic exam still outstanding
checks.value: "Pull mixed liquor sample for SVI exam" due 14:45, not done.
checks.why: Only a mixed-liquor exam separates filaments from the other causes of poor settling, and that decides the fix. This is why the conclusion stops at medium.

references.title: Filamentous bulking, confirmed on the microscope
references.description: SVI climbs steadily over a day or two past 150 mL/g, the blanket deepens, TSS carryover follows, and the exam shows filaments bridging the floc. The fix depends on which organism: more RAS and a selector, or RAS chlorination.
notes: Same slow steady climb (+9.3 mL/g per hour here)
Same quiet RAS and mechanism
The exam is what separates this from the variant below

references.title: Deflocculation or dispersed growth
references.description: A toxic slug or a sudden nutrient shortage breaks the floc up. SVI rises faster and flattens, and the overflow goes cloudy out of proportion to the SVI because fine solids never settle at all. The exam shows no filaments.
notes: That rise is faster and then flattens; today's is still climbing
TSS removal here fell 1.6 points, in proportion to the SVI

references.title: Settleometer or sampling error
references.description: The sample is taken from a different point, or the cylinder is read late. SVI steps to a new level and stays there, and nothing else in the plant agrees with it.
notes: Here the largest 5-minute change is 1.26 mL/g — a curve, not a step
Here secondary TSS removal fell with it

ruledOut.cause: RAS rate too low for the inventory
ruledOut.reason: RAS trended +0.14 % per hour — flat — and stayed inside the 25–75 % range. Nothing on the return side moved while the SVI climbed 47 mL/g.

ruledOut.cause: Clarifier mechanism or hydraulic overload
ruledOut.reason: Torque 46.0–56.1 % with no trend (+0.08 points per hour). A dragging rake or a deepening blanket would load the drive.

ruledOut.cause: A loading or MLSS change
ruledOut.reason: MLSS 2,559–3,040 mg/L and F:M 0.258–0.313 in this train, both inside the conventional bands, and sludge age steady at 8.9 days.

ruledOut.cause: An SVI test or analyser error
ruledOut.reason: Secondary TSS removal, measured separately, fell 1.6 points over the same hours, and the climb is smooth (largest step 1.26 mL/g). A test problem would step and nothing else would agree.

ruledOut.cause: Low DO driving filamentous growth
ruledOut.reason: The classic trigger, and worth asking the lab about: T01 aeration averaged 1.61 mg/L over the last 2 hours, the lowest of the six trains, though it never spent more than 15 min under 1.5 mg/L. The timing is wrong for it to be the trigger — the SVI left its baseline at 09:20, hours before the DO reached its lowest — but it could be feeding the trend now.

chart.caption: DO in this basin against the range in the other five.

ruledOut.cause: Nutrient deficiency or a septic influent
ruledOut.reason: Influent nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphide are not instrumented in this model, and all six trains share the influent, so a plant-wide nutrient cause would have moved the other five clarifiers too. The exam will see the organism either way.

confidence.because: SVI and secondary TSS removal are separate measurements and both moved the same way, while RAS, mechanism torque and the whole aeration side held still.
confidence.notHigherBecause: Nobody has looked at the mixed liquor under a microscope. From trends alone, filaments, dispersed growth and a nutrient shortage all look like a rising SVI.
confidence.raiseIf: The exam finds filaments bridging the floc, or the SVI passes 150 mL/g with the blanket deepening.
confidence.lowerIf: The exam is clean and the SVI flattens. Then treat it as normal sludge variation and re-sample next shift.

action.text: Pull a mixed liquor sample for microscopic exam; consider a small RAS rate increase if SVI continues climbing past 150.

WSIT09.impact: At +9.3 mL/g per hour it reaches the 150 mL/g bulking level in about 51 min, around 14:56. Secondary TSS removal has already lost 1.6 points.

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: The T05 Sludge Collector stopped under load at 10:20; the solids carryover, the rising blanket and the extra load on aeration all followed from it
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: removal came straight back when the flights moved again

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: Primary TSS removal on T05 against its level before the stop and the other five trains. T05 lost 23 points in 15 min and came back within 25 min of the stop.

checks.label: Sludge Collector went from running to stopped in one interval
checks.value: Motor current 5.75 → 0.00 A and travel speed 44.6 → 0.0 % at 10:20; stopped for 15 min, running again at 10:35 at 6.11 A.
checks.why: Zero current with zero travel is a stopped drive, not a slow one. A worn chain or a dragging flight loses speed over hours; a drive that trips does it between two samples.

checks.label: TSS removal fell as soon as it stopped
checks.value: 60.5 % over the 30 min before the stop down to 38.0 % at 10:35 (−22.5 points) — past the 10-point flag level at 10:30.
checks.why: The collector is what takes settled sludge out of the tank. With it stopped the sludge stays put, the effective depth shrinks, and solids leave over the weirs within minutes.

checks.label: Sludge blanket rose at the same time
checks.value: 35.5 % before the stop to 44.1 % at 10:35 (+8.6 points); flag level is +5 points within 45 min.
checks.why: Sludge still arrives while nothing is being pulled out, so the blanket climbs toward the weirs. This is the mechanism, measured on a separate instrument from the TSS removal.

checks.label: The drive was already working too hard
checks.value: Peak current 5.75 A in the 30 min before the stop against a running median of 5.07 A (+13 %); 6.11 A on the restart, easing off after.
checks.why: Heavy sludge or debris under the flights loads the drive before the overload device lets go. A current climb and then a trip is the mechanical story; an electrical fault drops out with no warning.

checks.label: It happened at the top of the day's flow
checks.value: T05 influent 292 gpm at 10:20 — the 81st percentile of the day's readings (day range 257–308 gpm).
checks.why: More flow means more solids arriving and more drag on the flights, which is why these drives trip during the late-morning peak and not at 04:00.

checks.label: BOD removal followed it down
checks.value: Primary BOD removal 30.3 → 26.6 % (−3.8 points) over the same window.
checks.why: A separate measurement. Much of the BOD a primary removes rides on the settleable solids, so BOD removal has to move with TSS removal. It rules out a TSS analyser problem.

checks.label: The other five trains took the same peak and held
checks.value: T01, T02, T03, T04 and T06 lost at most 7.6 points of TSS removal over the same window (T02 worst), against 22.5 points here, on flows in the 15–78th percentile of their own day.
checks.why: The whole plant saw the same morning peak. If the flow alone were enough, every primary would have lost solids. Only the one with the stopped collector did.

checks.label: Extra load turned up in aeration behind it
checks.value: T05 aeration F:M +0.021 and DO −0.30 mg/L within 1 h of the stop. For scale, the other five aeration stages moved +0.016 to +0.034 on F:M over the same window.
checks.why: Following the process-flow edge from the primary basin to the aeration basin: solids that escape the primary arrive as organic load a stage later. Honest caveat — the morning peak alone moves F:M by about as much on the other trains, so this is consistent with the stall, not proof of it.

checks.label: Back to normal once it was restarted
checks.value: Running again at 10:35 (15 min after the stop); TSS removal back to 59.0 % at 10:45, the blanket back to 34.3 % after. "Clarifier drive chain inspection" completed 10:40.
checks.why: Removal returning as soon as the flights moved again ties the solids loss to the collector and to nothing in the influent.

references.title: Drive overload trip at peak flow, restarted by hand
references.description: Current climbs for a few minutes as heavy sludge builds under the flights, the overload device lets go, and removal falls about a point a minute. An operator clears the obstruction and restarts; removal is back inside half an hour. The follow-up is chain tension and shear-pin condition before the next peak.
notes: Same drive current climb before the stop (+13 %)
Same fall and the same recovery after 15 min

references.title: Collector left out of service
references.description: The same trip, but nobody restarts it. The blanket keeps climbing, solids go over the weirs for hours, and the day's TSS average is at risk. The aeration basin takes the whole primary load.
notes: Stopped for 15 min here, not hours
Blanket peaked at 44 % and came back

charts.title: Primary TSS removal (min from the stop)

references.title: Hydraulic surge with the collector running
references.description: A wet-weather or pump-station surge shortens the detention time in every primary at once. Removal dips a few points across the plant and recovers as the flow eases. The collector never stops and the blanket barely moves.
notes: Here the collector current went to 0.00 A
Here T05 lost 23 points while the other five lost at most 7.6

charts.title: Primary TSS removal (min from the stop)

ruledOut.cause: A hydraulic surge on its own
ruledOut.reason: The other five primaries were on flows between the 15th and 78th percentile of their own day at the same moment and lost at most 7.6 points of removal. T05 lost 22.5.

ruledOut.cause: A weir, scum or skimmer problem
ruledOut.reason: Scum removal held 94.4 → 92.5 % through the event and the Scum Skimmer drew 4.56–4.87 A with no interruption.

ruledOut.cause: A TSS analyser fault
ruledOut.reason: Three other instruments moved with it: the blanket level (+8.6 points by 10:35), primary BOD removal (−3.8 points) and the collector's own motor current. A bad analyser moves alone.

ruledOut.cause: A solids loading change from upstream
ruledOut.reason: T05 influent flow was 292 gpm, inside the day's 257–308 gpm range, and removal was back to 59.0 % within 25 min of the restart with no change upstream.

ruledOut.cause: Why the drive tripped — shear pin, chain or debris
ruledOut.reason: The drive's own fault code and a look at the chain tension will say which. The current climb to 5.75 A before the stop and 6.11 A on the restart point at mechanical load rather than an electrical fault.

confidence.because: The collector stopped and TSS removal, the blanket level and BOD removal all moved with it, and all three came back within 25 min of the restart.
confidence.lowerIf: Removal stays low with the collector running. Then look at the weirs, the flow split and the influent solids.

action.text: Log for the peak-flow maintenance review; inspect drive chain tension before the next peak flow period.

WSIT10.impact: 25 min from stop to full recovery, with removal down to 38 % at the worst point — 23 points of solids past the primary, during the day's peak flow. The blanket reached 44 % and the aeration basin behind it saw F:M +0.021.

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: T02's RAS rate was left on 38.7 % while the incoming load rose, so F:M climbed to 0.350 and the solids inventory thinned
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed: F:M and MLSS answered the RAS change

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: T02's F:M ratio against its RAS rate (shown ÷ 100 to share the axis). The load rose from 10:30; RAS did not move until 12:10, and F:M came back inside the band within 10 min.

checks.label: F:M above the 0.32 target ceiling and holding
checks.value: 0.278 at 10:30 climbing to 0.350 at 12:05; above 0.32 from 11:35. Flagged at 12:05, after 30 min over the ceiling.
checks.why: Conventional activated sludge runs at an F:M of about 0.20–0.32 d⁻¹. Above that the bugs are overfed: settling gets worse and effluent BOD follows.

checks.label: A steady climb, not a blip
checks.value: +0.072 over 1 h 35 min, from the low point at 10:30. Flag level is +0.040 over 2 h.
checks.why: F:M is organic load divided by the solids holding it. A steady rise means one of the two moved and stayed moved.

checks.label: RAS rate sat on one number the whole time
checks.value: 38.8 % with a standard deviation of 0.21 points over the 2 h F:M spent climbing, against 1.08–1.55 points on the other five trains' quietest two hours.
checks.why: RAS is the operator's handle on the solids inventory. A rate this steady is a manual setpoint nobody moved, not a controller following the load.

checks.label: The blowers could see the extra load
checks.value: Header air 4,273 → 4,612 scfm (+7.9 %) over the same hours, on a DO controller that was holding its setpoint.
checks.why: An independent read on the load: oxygen demand goes with organic load, so a DO controller that has to push more air is telling us the load really did rise. It is not an F:M calculation artefact.

checks.label: Solids inventory never built to meet the load
checks.value: MLSS 2,948 mg/L when the climb started against 2,716 mg/L at the F:M peak, bottoming at 2,661 mg/L. Holding F:M would have needed it to build.
checks.why: Holding F:M steady under a rising load means returning more solids. With RAS fixed, the inventory drifts the wrong way and F:M rises twice as fast — numerator up, denominator down.

checks.label: Incoming flow rose with it
checks.value: T02 influent 296 → 311 gpm (+5.0 %) over the drift.
checks.why: A third measurement on the load side, upstream of everything else. More flow at the same strength is more load into the basin.

checks.label: Not an air or DO problem
checks.value: DO held 1.78–2.35 mg/L right through, above the 1.5 mg/L floor.
checks.why: If aeration had been the problem, DO would have fallen as the load rose. It did not: the air side kept up. What did not keep up was the sludge return.

checks.label: Not a settling or bulking problem
checks.value: T02 SVI 110–130 mL/g all shift, below the 130 mL/g watch level.
checks.why: Bulking sludge would also raise F:M, by losing solids over the weirs. Settleability never moved here, so the solids are in the system — just not being returned fast enough.

checks.label: The other five trains kept RAS moving
checks.value: T01, T03, T04, T05 and T06: RAS standard deviation 1.08–1.55 points over two hours, and none of them held F:M above 0.32 for more than 5 min (flag level 30 min).
checks.why: Same influent, same diurnal curve, same rising load. The five trains whose RAS followed the load never left the F:M band. That is the comparison that makes this a control miss.

checks.label: F:M and MLSS answered the RAS change
checks.value: RAS 38.7 → 45.6 % at 12:10; RAS pump flow 280 → 315 gpm (+12 %) and motor current 24.5 → 26.6 A; MLSS built 2,661 → 3,236 mg/L and F:M was back under 0.32 by 12:20 (10 min after the change).
checks.why: The test of the whole explanation: move the one input the detector blames and the output has to follow. It did, on four instruments — RAS rate, pump flow, pump current and MLSS.

references.title: Manual RAS setpoint left behind a load ramp
references.description: The diurnal load climbs through the morning, RAS stays where the night shift left it, and F:M walks out of the band while MLSS thins. Raising RAS brings both back within the hour. The lasting fix is flow-pacing RAS off the influent signal.
notes: Same flat RAS (0.21 points of standard deviation here)
Same MLSS sliding while F:M rose
Same quick answer to the RAS change (10 min)

charts.title: F:M ratio (h from the load rise)

references.title: RAS pump losing capacity
references.description: The setpoint is being chased, but the pump cannot make it: the rate command moves while actual flow and motor current do not, and F:M drifts anyway. A worn impeller or a partly blocked suction. The giveaway is a RAS rate that moves without the flow following.
notes: Here RAS never moved at all until it was raised by hand
Here pump flow followed the change (+12 %)

charts.title: F:M ratio (h from the load rise)

references.title: MLSS analyser drifting low
references.description: F:M is calculated from MLSS, so an analyser reading low invents an F:M rise out of nothing. Air flow and influent flow stay flat, and a lab MLSS disagrees with the online reading.
notes: Here header air rose +7.9 % — the load was real
Here MLSS answered the RAS change (+574 mg/L)

charts.title: F:M ratio (h from the load rise)

ruledOut.cause: An MLSS analyser error
ruledOut.reason: Two independent load signals rose with the F:M: header air +7.9 % and T02 influent flow +5.0 %. And MLSS built +574 mg/L the moment RAS was raised, which a drifting analyser would not do.

ruledOut.cause: A load spike with RAS tracking it correctly
ruledOut.reason: RAS held 38.8 % with 0.21 points of standard deviation over two hours while the other five trains moved 1.08–1.55 points and none of them held F:M over the ceiling for more than 5 min.

ruledOut.cause: An air or DO shortfall
ruledOut.reason: DO never went below 1.78 mg/L and the header air rose to meet the demand. The air side was the part that worked.

ruledOut.cause: Bulking sludge losing solids over the weirs
ruledOut.reason: T02 SVI 110–130 mL/g, below the 130 mL/g watch level, and clarifier torque gave no sign of a deep blanket.

ruledOut.cause: Wasting too hard (WAS set too high)
ruledOut.reason: Sludge age held 9.1–10.6 days, inside the conventional 5–15 day range, so the inventory was not being thrown away. WAS flow itself is not instrumented in this model — the sludge-age trend is the proxy.

ruledOut.cause: Why the setpoint was left behind
ruledOut.reason: Whether RAS is on a manual setpoint by design or an auto flow-pacing loop failed is not in the data. The RAS rate review on the work list is where that answer comes from.

confidence.because: Three independent instruments say the load rose (F:M, header air, influent flow), the RAS rate was measurably flat against five trains that were not, and F:M and MLSS both answered within 10 min of the RAS change.
confidence.lowerIf: F:M stays high after RAS is raised. Then suspect the RAS pump's delivery, or a lab MLSS that disagrees with the online analyser.
confidence.confirmedBy: F:M back under 0.32 within 10 min of the RAS change

action.text: Adjust RAS rate to track incoming load more responsively; review the auto-adjustment logic if available.

WSIT11.impact: 45 min above the F:M ceiling, peaking at 0.350, with MLSS 2,661 mg/L at its thinnest. Sustained, that is where poor settling and effluent BOD start; it was caught before the SVI moved.

conclusion.label: What's needed
conclusion.text: Pull the final effluent sample while the index is flat at 13.7 (6.3 under the 20 limit) and file the DMR by 15:30
conclusion.confidenceText: A margin and a deadline, not a diagnosis

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: T04's fecal coliform risk index against what the (CT₀/CT)² relationship alone would predict, and the other five trains. The gap is the part shorter contact time does not explain.

checks.label: Still inside the limit, with 6.3 of margin
checks.value: Worst sample in the last 1 h 14.8 against a limit of 20; the day's peak was 14.8 at 14:00 (5.2 of margin). 6.3 (32 % of the limit) left on the half-hour average now.
checks.why: Nothing is out of compliance. The flag is that the margin has gone under 40 % of the limit, which is where a single bad grab sample stops being academic.

checks.label: This train is taking more of the plant's flow
checks.value: T04's share of the six trains' throughput +4.2 % over the last 1 h against the rest of the shift, while T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 moved −1.7 to +0.3 %. Contact time −1.1 % on +3.8 % more treated flow.
checks.why: Comparing shares removes the plant-wide diurnal curve: the rest of the plant is coming off its morning peak and this train is not. More flow through the same contact basin is less contact time, and that is the mechanism behind the number.

checks.label: Disinfection itself is in order
checks.value: Chlorine residual averaging 0.65 mg/L over the last 1 h (range 0.61–0.69), inside the 0.5–1.0 mg/L band; CT averaging 65.3 against a baseline of 67.1 (−2.7 %), inside the 15 % band.
checks.why: This separates a compliance item from a fault. The feed pump is holding its residual and the contact basin is giving its CT; the equipment is doing its job.

checks.label: Running above where the shift started
checks.value: 9.7 over the first 3 h against 13.7 on the last 30 min (+4.0), peaking at 14.8 at 14:00. The half-hour average has been above 11.2 since 13:10 (55 min).
checks.why: The absolute level is each train's own; a step up against this stage's own morning is what makes today's sample worth watching. Reading the half-hour average keeps single noisy samples out of it.

checks.label: Shorter contact explains part of it, not all
checks.value: Risk goes as (CT₀/CT)². CT was −6.9 % at 14:00, which accounts for +1.5 of the +5.2 rise at that point; 3.7 is left over, and the half-hour average of the leftover is +2.9 now against a flag level of 0.8.
checks.why: A physics model with nothing fitted: CT is residual × contact time, and disinfection kill goes as the square of CT. The part the arithmetic cannot explain is solids and load carried through from upstream, shielding organisms from the chlorine.

checks.label: Borderline, not running away
checks.value: +2.0 per hour over the last hour, +2.4 per hour over the last 2 h. Flag level for "stable" is under 3 per hour.
checks.why: This is what makes it a reporting decision rather than a developing failure: the index stepped up and then sat there. A failure would keep climbing.

checks.label: It is this train's own, not the whole plant
checks.value: T04's flow share is +4.2 % against +0.3 % for the next-highest train, and it is +4.0 off its own baseline against +2.1 for T05, the nearest of the other five (range −2.1 to +2.1).
checks.why: All six trains discharge the same day's effluent. A plant-wide shift would be a different conversation with the regulator; one train is a sampling and reporting question. The flow share is the cleaner comparison — the risk index wanders by a point or two on its own.

checks.label: Discharge end in order
checks.value: Dechlorinated residual 0.033–0.077 mg/L, under 0.15 mg/L all shift.
checks.why: A separate instrument at the end of the line. The bisulfite is doing its job, so the coliform number is not an artefact of chlorine still being in the sample.

checks.label: 1 h 25 min to the filing deadline, about 40 min of work
checks.value: "Prepare DMR filing" due 15:30, not done; 40 min of work with 45 min of slack. The final effluent sample has to be pulled before that.
checks.why: The deadline is not the binding constraint today — the number that goes on the form is. Once the sample is taken the reported value is fixed, so the sample timing matters more than the filing time.

references.title: Borderline day reported, and defended
references.description: The index steps up with the afternoon flow and flattens well inside the limit. The operator pulls an extra grab sample, notes the flow and contact time on the bench sheet, and files the DMR on time. The margin is documented, so the number is defensible even if the next sample is worse.
notes: Same step-and-flatten shape (+2.0 per hour now)
Same intact CT (−2.7 %)
1 h 25 min left for 40 min of work

The filing task is already open on the list

references.title: Real loss of disinfection
references.description: A chlorine feed pump air-locking or a short-circuiting contact basin. The risk index climbs the same way, but the residual sags and CT falls hard with it, and the index keeps going past the limit. That is a fault, with a different response.
notes: Here residual held 0.61–0.69 mg/L
Here CT only moved −2.7 %

charts.title: Fecal coliform risk index (min from the step up)

ruledOut.cause: Lost disinfection — feed pump, residual or contact time
ruledOut.reason: Chlorine residual stayed 0.61–0.69 mg/L inside its band and CT averaged −2.7 %, well within the 15 % band. The dose is being delivered.

chart.caption: CT held through the elevated period.

ruledOut.cause: A chlorine overfeed masked by dechlorination
ruledOut.reason: Dechlorinated residual 0.033–0.077 mg/L and the chlorine residual never went above 0.70 mg/L. Nothing is being over-dosed and hidden.

ruledOut.cause: A plant-wide effluent shift
ruledOut.reason: Every other train's share of the plant flow moved −1.7 to +0.3 % against +4.2 % here, and T04 is the furthest off its own baseline (+4.0 against +2.1 for T05). One train moved.

ruledOut.cause: An analyser fault on the risk index
ruledOut.reason: The rise is partly accounted for by measured CT (+1.5 of +5.2), so at least part of it is arithmetic off two other instruments. A grab sample settles the rest, which is what the recommendation asks for.

ruledOut.cause: Where the extra load came from
ruledOut.reason: Influent strength and effluent TSS are not instrumented in this model. The 2.9 the CT arithmetic cannot explain is consistent with solids carried through at +3.8 % more treated flow, but the grab sample and the secondary clarifier bench sheet are what confirm it.

confidence.because: Everything here is read straight off instruments: the index against its own morning, the margin against the permit limit, the residual and CT against their bands, and the filing time off the work list. The only inference is the (CT₀/CT)² split, and it is arithmetic, not a diagnosis.
